market_holds: Spot $1.38 at the 2026-11-13 seal: a 52-week low, 78% below the 52-week high, -10.4% over 5 days, -12.1% over 20 and -41.8% over 60 (Yahoo daily bars). There is no usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided), so no implied move. The baseline's 2.44% 'usual move' comes from non-earnings 6-K matches and should not be used. The real reactions on the last four results days, close to close from Yahoo bars, were Q3'25 (2025-11-13) -7.0%, Q4'25 (2026-03-11) +9.1%, Q1'26 (2026-05-05) +31.6% on 20m shares, and Q2'26 (2026-07-31) -4.3%. Median absolute move is about 8%. Consensus for Q3 from secondary aggregators, with unclear ages: EPS about -$0.04 to -$0.05; revenue $29.6m (Benzinga), $32.7m (Earnings Whispers), average $36m with a $30m low (StockAlarm). Revenue missed in Q1 ($19.4m vs $20.2m) and badly in Q2 ($20.6m vs about $26-27m). Management guided 2026 revenue 'back-half weighted' (about 60% in H2 per a call summary), opex $65-75m standalone and capex $5-10m. The Oct-22 Forum set a 30% revenue CAGR for two years, gross margin above 20% in 2027 and above 25% in 2028, adjusted EBITDA positive by end-2027, and $80-120m of HPU fleet capex, mostly asset-financed. The sell side is drifting down: BMO Underperform with a $1.50 target (from $2.10, 2026-10-26); Susquehanna cut to $2 (Neutral, 2026-10-14). Short interest is 20.7m shares, about 5.9% of shares, 8 days to cover (FINRA 2026-10-30): not a crowded short. The run-in is the hydrogen/fuel-cell basket. On most days of the last three weeks BLDP moved with PLUG, FCEL and BE, which swing 5-15% a day (e.g. 11-05: BLDP -8.2, FCEL -15.3, BE -16.4). On the seal day BLDP fell 1.5% while PLUG fell 10.9%. GeoPura closed 2026-08-28 (£82.5m cash plus about 49.6m shares). The business acquisition report filed this morning (6-K 2026-11-13) shows GeoPura's FY to Mar-26 revenue of £7.3m and net loss of £50.7m, and Apr-Jun 2026 revenue of £29.6m (mostly a one-off facility or inventory sale) with a net loss of £16.1m. Its pro forma goodwill is $111.6m on $230.7m of consideration. The stock barely reacted to that filing.
view: This is the first quarter that includes GeoPura (from Aug 28) in the consolidated numbers. That makes the headline messy and the comparison to consensus noisy. My revenue arithmetic: the 2026 shape (H1 $40.0m, about 60% back-half) implies about $60m for H2. Converting the Q2 12-month order book ($74.4m) at the last four quarters' rate of 36-47% gives about $27-35m, central $30m. That is in line with the $29.6-33m consensus, not clearly beside it. Two adjustments pull the other way. GeoPura's 154-module order sat in Q2 intake and in the order book, and deliveries to it after Aug 28 are now intercompany and drop out of revenue and backlog. On the other side, GeoPura's own September revenue is added. Below revenue, adding GeoPura's losses (about £11m a quarter at the operating level in Apr-Jun) plus acquisition costs, at the new share count, makes an 'EPS/loss wider than expected' headline more likely than not against -$0.04/-$0.05. Opex guidance will likely rise on consolidation. The last two prints missed and drew -4.3%. Against that, the stock is at a 52-week low with market cap about $486m against Q3 cash of very roughly $380m after the deal cash. Expectations are already deflated: BMO's $1.50 target is the spot price. Two of the last four prints rallied hard (+9%, +32%) on margin and narrative, and the call introduces the EaaS/data-centre HPU story with GeoPura's president. A reaction inside the window (close Friday to 13:00 Monday) also carries the hydrogen basket's Monday tape, which alone moves this name 5%+ on ordinary days. I lean slightly down, but nothing I found shows the deciding line (revenue against a back-half guide, or margins) landing on one side of what the price holds. This is a no-call.

recommendation.reason: My own revenue arithmetic from the order book and the back-half guide lands on the stale-ish consensus, not beside it. The negatives I can see (GeoPura losses consolidating, intercompany eliminations, acquisition costs, two straight misses) are public, and they come into a stock already at its 52-week low and at the most bearish analyst's target. The hydrogen basket's daily swings are as large as any company-specific gap I could build, so I cannot show an unpriced direction at 65% or better.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 revenue at $35m or more with gross margin held at or above 20%, plus a lowered standalone opex run-rate, would make an up move likely despite the consolidation noise. Revenue near $25m with a backlog decline would make the down case.

self_critique: The case for up is real. The stock sits at its 52-week low and at the bear's target. Market cap is little above post-deal cash. Results days have produced +9% and +32% rallies from depressed levels when margins surprised. Q3 is the seasonally strong, back-half-weighted quarter. The new EaaS/data-centre story gets its first full airing on Monday's call. A loss widened by consolidation is easy for the market to look through as non-recurring. Against my small lean down, the Monday sector tape could swamp everything either way.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped most: the name moves with the fuel-cell basket, so the run-up says nothing company-specific. P3's 'own arithmetic' (order-book conversion) let me test the consensus rather than trust it. P4 kept me from treating the newly filed GeoPura losses as unpriced when the stock had outperformed peers on the filing day. The baseline's history (6-K matches) was useless, and the real earnings reactions had to be rebuilt by hand.
